question: What should the first OpenClaw-owned skill permission manifest contract include, and how should declared permissions relate to install consent, ClawHub trust, signing, attestation, and runtime enforcement?
rationale: The remaining work defines a public skill ecosystem security contract and trust boundary; automation cannot safely choose schema placement, trust roots, consent semantics, or declared-versus-enforced wording.

options.title: Consolidate Design First
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security design anchor and use the related RFCs and open PR as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

options.title: Land Audit-Only Metadata First
options.body: Approve a narrow optional manifest that is explicitly inspect-only, then track consent, signing, attestation, and enforcement as separate phases.

options.title: Route To ClawHub Policy
options.body: Let ClawHub or governance plugins own declarations and trust scoring unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Consolidate Design First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security design anchor and use the related RFCs and open PR as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest human keep-open review and adjacent security/docs history make this the best available decision owner from the identified routing candidates.
